clue.text: Manipulates schemes to secure a couple of grand?

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the schemes enclose the pair of thousands

parts.note: wiles are cunning schemes or tricks
G is slang for a grand (a thousand pounds or dollars); a couple of them gives two Gs

explanation.surface: A schemer pulls strings to pocket a couple of thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To wiggle something is to move it about by small adjustments, a physical sense of working or handling it.

clue.text: Revolutionary account after gathering of women produces witchcraft

indicators.note: after puts the turned account later than the women's gathering

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the account abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A rebel's report from a women's meeting reveals witchcraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women, famous for jam and Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is a modern pagan religion based on traditional witchcraft.

clue.text: Apparently unknown to invest in equipment in period when not studying

indicators.note: to invest is to put money into, so the two pieces are placed inside the equipment

parts.note: gear is equipment or kit
ap. is taken as an abbreviation for apparently
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Something apparently unknown is put into kit for a break from study.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap year is a year out, usually between school and university, spent travelling or working rather than at college.

clue.text: Look — Dame receiving credit and influence? On the contrary

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, signalling that one piece is put inside another
on the contrary reverses who receives whom, so the credit and influence words take in the Dame

parts.note: a loan is credit extended to someone
hold is power or influence over someone
DBE is Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A Dame is offered credit and sway, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, DBE would hold LOAN and HOLD; 'On the contrary' flips it so LOAN and HOLD surround DBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo and behold is an exclamation drawing attention to something surprising, like look.

clue.text: Issue lowest type of poem

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
net, after all deductions, is the lowest figure for an amount

explanation.surface: Someone publishes the most basic sort of poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem, a particular form of verse.

clue.text: Extreme concern about the aspect of a vulture, say

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for extreme concern wraps round the next word

parts.note: fear is extreme anxiety or concern
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply worried by how a vulture looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like part of the definition, but it is the piece placed inside FEAR. 'say' marks the vulture as just one example of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulture, like any bird, is covered in plumage, so one plume is a part or aspect of it.

clue.text: Came out, satisfied about cow?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the satisfied word goes round the cow

parts.note: fed means satisfied, having eaten
a cow lows, so it is a lower; the question mark flags the made-up noun

explanation.surface: Someone confessed, content about a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came out' suggests a confession, but means bloomed. LOWER is not 'less high' but 'one that lows', i.e. moos.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has flowered has come out into bloom.

clue.text: Skill but no power in actor's role

indicators.note: but no means without, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An actor's role needs skill but no force.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean skill or knack, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Helium and phosphorus affected neat hydrocarbon

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of neat are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two elements change a pure hydrocarbon, chemistry-style.
explanation.definitionFit: Heptane is an alkane with seven carbon atoms, a hydrocarbon found in petrol.

clue.text: Something that echoes treason or showing corruption

indicators.note: corruption means being spoilt, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An echoing device reveals treason or graft.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonator is a body that vibrates in sympathy, amplifying or prolonging sound.

clue.text: Pirate chief likely to be throttled by murderer

indicators.note: throttled means gripped round the neck, so the murderer's name surrounds the word for likely

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis, the first murderer
apt means likely or inclined (apt to do something)

explanation.surface: A pirate leader seems likely to be strangled by a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate ship's commander is its captain, as with Captain Hook or Captain Kidd.

clue.text: Far-reaching figure's work seen after 31 days

indicators.note: seen after puts the word for work later than the month in the answer

parts.note: October has 31 days, abbreviated Oct
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A wide-ranging person's achievement appears at the end of a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of figure's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus, with its eight long arms, is a creature that reaches far; the word is also used for sprawling organisations.

clue.text: Promotion retaining workers? That's better

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the promotion keeps the workers inside it

parts.note: an ad (advertisement) promotes a product
men can mean workers, as in employers and men

explanation.surface: An employee hopes a promotion that keeps the staff on will improve things.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or improve, so an amended version is a better one.

clue.text: Certainly may be evidenced in wrecked retina — this?

definitions.text: Certainly may be evidenced in wrecked retina — this?

indicators.note: evidenced in means seen within, so the word for certainly sits inside the shuffled letters
wrecked means ruined, so the letters of retina are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly

explanation.surface: A damaged retina could show this strain, the clue asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges the letters into E TRAIN. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a strained, overworked retina is exactly where this condition would show.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, overworked eyes show their strain, a condition that a damaged retina could well display.

clue.text: It's a moving effect when you think about it

definitions.text: It's a moving effect when you think about it

parts.words: It's a moving effect when you think about it
parts.note: the phrase sounds like praise for something touching, but means an effect that moves objects purely by thinking

explanation.surface: A remark that something is touching once you reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed power to move objects by mental effort alone is a psychic phenomenon.

clue.text: Arrives in big city finding network of streets

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for arrives inside the word for big city

parts.note: wen is a nickname for a big city, from Cobbett's 'the Great Wen' for London
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: Someone reaches a large city and finds a maze of streets.
explanation.walkthrough: WEN, a crossword favourite, comes from William Cobbett calling London 'the Great Wen' (a swelling).
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a crowded maze of narrow streets, by figurative extension from a rabbits' burrow system.

clue.text: Water source with low temperature, intended as a good thing

parts.note: a well is a source of water
mean can mean low or base

explanation.surface: A cool spring was meant to be beneficial.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-meant action is kindly intended, even if it misfires.

clue.text: Man is going to risk capturing knight recklessly

parts.note: he'll is short for he will, a man is going to

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so the wager holds the knight inside it

parts.note: to bet is to risk money on an outcome
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A gambler is about to wager wildly, chess pieces and all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means fiercely determined whatever the consequences, so going ahead heedlessly and with abandon.

clue.text: What may have produced roaring sound intermingled with air?

indicators.note: intermingled means mixed together, so the two words' letters are blended into one order

explanation.surface: The clue asks what made a roar mixed into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roaring sound' reads as one phrase, but 'roaring' ends the definition and 'sound' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric reptiles such as T. rex are popularly pictured bellowing, so one could have made the noise.

clue.text: Like electrons, for example, damaging to pencil

indicators.note: damaging means breaking, so the letters of the words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Electrons could harm a pencil, the clue jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrons belong to the lepton family of light particles, so they have a lepton-related character.

clue.text: Bird seen in nut tree around Long Island

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the nut tree wraps the island's letters

parts.note: the pecan is a hickory tree bearing nuts
LI is the standard abbreviation for Long Island, New York

explanation.surface: A bird perches in a nut tree on Long Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a throat pouch for scooping fish.

clue.text: Be very critical about series about garden location

indicators.note: the second about means surrounding, so the series abbreviation goes round the garden place

parts.note: Kew, in west London, is home to the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: A critic harshly reviews a TV series set around a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' belongs to the definition; the second is the container. Kew Gardens is the famous botanic garden in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To skewer someone is to attack them mercilessly in criticism, as if running them through on a spike.

clue.text: Outfit in part of London street appearing in a short time

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so the street abbreviation sits within the time word

parts.note: a while is a short time

explanation.surface: A suit turns up quickly on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'whistle and flute' means suit, shortened to whistle; 'part of London' points to the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is a suit of clothes, an outfit, in the rhyming slang of London's East End.

clue.text: Reliable about time, not easily distracted

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reliable word goes round the time letter

parts.note: solid means dependable or reliable

explanation.surface: A dependable, punctual person keeps focused.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is impassive and unexcitable, so calm and hard to sidetrack.

clue.text: Endless sickness and decline keeping one insensitive?

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter, so the illness word loses its end

parts.note: a malady is an illness

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the decline word contains the one

parts.note: rot is decay or decline
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A long illness and decline leave a patient numb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops Y from MALADY to give MALAD. The question mark admits that insensitive here means tactless, not physically numb.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy, especially socially tactless, which is a kind of insensitivity in dealing with people.

clue.text: Fixes trouble between bridge partners

indicators.note: between places the trouble word in the middle of the two partners

parts.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table, giving N and S
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A bridge pair sorts out a problem between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten it in place, so fixes is a synonym verb in the same form.

clue.text: Emblem of justice, showing promise given to Society

indicators.note: given to means attached to, so the promise word joins after the society letter

parts.note: giving your word is making a promise

explanation.surface: A symbol of justice appears when a pledge is made to a society.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues of Justice hold scales and a blade, so the blade is her emblem.

clue.text: Bounder interrupting song in Stoppard play

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the bounder goes inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a bounder, an ungentlemanly man

explanation.surface: A cad cuts into a song during a Tom Stoppard production.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia (1993) is one of Tom Stoppard's best-known plays, set in a country house.

clue.text: Exhaust Government tracker

parts.note: to do someone in, or be done, means to exhaust; do alone can mean tire out

explanation.surface: A government official trails exhaust fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, and as a noun a dog is a tracking animal.

clue.text: He's too upset to go to lake in African country

indicators.note: to go to means joining on after, so the jumble follows the lake letter

parts.note: L is a map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man is too distressed to visit a lake in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountainous kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Organiser needing time to replace minute bird

indicators.note: to replace means taking the place of, so the time letter swaps in for the minute letter

parts.note: a manager organises things

explanation.surface: A busy organiser needs time in place of a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: The tanager is a brightly coloured American songbird, so a particular kind of bird.

clue.text: Incline to follow detectives in balloon

indicators.note: to follow means coming after, so the incline word comes after the detectives

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to tend is to incline towards something

explanation.surface: Detectives are drawn to follow a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: Balloon as a verb means swell out, and to distend is to swell from pressure within.
